title: WooCommerce emails not sending? Diagnose it in four steps

linkedin.post:
Your store just took a payment.

Your customer got nothing.

No receipt. No confirmation. Just silence.

And you would never know. Your dashboard says "paid." Everything looks fine.

Here is what is really going on:

Every order email passes through four hands.
Your store, WordPress, your host, then their inbox provider.

Any one of them can drop it. From the outside, all four look the same.

Most owners only find out when an angry customer writes in.

Three things worth checking today:

1️⃣ Is the order stuck at "pending payment"?
That sends nothing. By design.

2️⃣ Does your email record say "sent"?
That only means your store let go of it. Not that anyone got it.

3️⃣ Is anything marked "skipped"?
Often a blank recipient. No error. Just gone.

It takes ten minutes and one test order.

Which one has bitten your store?

instagram.caption:
🚨 Your dashboard says "paid." Your customer's inbox says nothing.

Both can be true on the same day.

Here are 3 facts that surprise most store owners:

1️⃣ Sent is not delivered
Your store's record only shows it passed the message along.

2️⃣ A stuck order sends nothing
Pending payment triggers no email. The money may be in, but the order never moved.

3️⃣ A blank recipient is skipped
No error. No email. Just a quiet gap in the record.

💡 One test order and one look at the record names the stage in minutes.

slides.sub: 4 stages to check, then when to call help

cards.label: Never triggered
cards.detail: Order status or email is off

cards.label: Landed in spam
cards.detail: Filed as junk by the inbox

slides.alt: Store owner at night with paid orders on screen while the phone inbox is empty and an envelope fades away.

slides.headline: Email Never Triggered
slides.body: The order never reached the point where an email fires, or the email is switched off or has no one to send to. Check this first.
slides.alt: A glowing envelope stopped behind a red barrier gate: the order email never triggered.

slides.headline: Store Tried, Email Not Sent
slides.body: Your store keeps a record of each attempt. It shows if the message went out or was skipped. Read it and you stop guessing.
slides.alt: A monitor log of green checks and one red failed row under a magnifying glass: the email was not sent.

slides.headline: Inbox Refused The Email
slides.body: The message left your store, but the receiving inbox said no. Send from an address on your own domain, not a free mail one.
slides.alt: A security guard at a velvet rope turning away an envelope with a mismatched badge: the inbox refused it.

slides.headline: Email Landed In Spam
slides.body: The inbox took it but filed it as junk, because it could not confirm the email came from you. Ask your host to check the proof is set.
slides.alt: An envelope falling into an overflowing junk bin in a dim basement: the email landed in spam.

slides.headline: When To Bring In A Developer
slides.body: Paid orders that never move forward, or the same fault returning, need one. Hand over your test results and the record.
slides.alt: A developer at a night desk with monitors as a glowing envelope reaches an inbox: bring in a developer.
